entities.summary: Ioannis Kolettis was a Greek politician who played a pivotal role in shaping Greek affairs from the Greek War of Independence through the early years of the Greek Kingdom. As Minister to France and serving twice as Prime Minister, Kolettis was instrumental in conceiving the Byzantine restorationist and irredentist Megali Idea, which became the core of Greek foreign policy until the early 20th century. This idea, born out of Kolettis' interactions with influential figures such as Prince Alexei Alexandrovich and Prince Mikhail Viktorovich, aimed to reunify the Greek and Byzantine nations and secure the nation's place among the great powers of Europe. Through his tireless efforts, Kolettis succeeded in creating a sense of national identity and unity, which had a lasting impact on Greek politics and foreign policy. The Megali Idea also influenced the development of Greek nationalism, with its emphasis on the nation's historical and cultural ties to the Byzantine Empire. Furthermore, Kolettis' vision for a unified Greece helped to establish the country as a major player in regional and international affairs, paving the way for its modern-day status as a European Union member state. Kolettis' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his ideas and policies continue to shape Greek politics and foreign policy to this day.
